title: A normal working day
summary: ik: the stem. jij, u, hij, zij: stem + t. wij, jullie, zij: the infinitive. Jij or je directly after the verb loses its t. Spell the stem as a Dutch word: maak, stop, reis.
explain:
The present tense (*de tegenwoordige tijd*) is the tense Dutch uses most: for what is happening now, for habits, for facts, and very often for the future too (`Morgen werk ik thuis`). There is only one present tense: `ik werk` is both "I work" and "I am working". Getting it right depends on one thing: finding the **stem** of the verb.

### The stem and the endings

Take the infinitive and remove `-en`. What is left is the stem: `werken → werk`.

| | werken | ending |
| ik | werk | stem |
| jij / je, u | werkt | stem + t |
| hij, zij / ze, het | werkt | stem + t |
| wij / we, jullie, zij / ze | werken | infinitive |

> Ik werk op een kantoor. — I work in an office.
> Mijn collega werkt thuis. — My colleague works from home.
> Wij werken van negen tot vijf. — We work from nine to five.

### Spelling the stem

The stem has to **sound** like the infinitive, and it has to look like a Dutch word. That gives three rules.

- **A long vowel is written double.** In `ma-ken` the `a` is long because its syllable is open. Without `-en` the syllable closes, so the vowel is doubled: `maken → maak`, `lopen → loop`, `praten → praat`, `sturen → stuur`.
- **A double consonant becomes single.** Apart from loanwords like `stress`, no Dutch word ends in two of the same consonant: `stoppen → stop`, `zeggen → zeg`, `beginnen → begin`.
- **v becomes f, z becomes s.** Apart from loanwords like `quiz`, no Dutch word ends in v or z: `leven → leef`, `schrijven → schrijf`, `reizen → reis`, `lezen → lees`.

> Ik maak eerst koffie. — I make coffee first.
> De vergadering begint om tien uur. — The meeting starts at ten o'clock.
> Hij reist veel voor zijn werk. — He travels a lot for his work.

In the plural the infinitive comes back, and with it the single vowel and the v or z: `ik lees, hij leest`, but `wij lezen`; `ik maak`, but `wij maken`.

### Stems that end in t or d

- A stem that ends in **t** never gets a second t: `praten → hij praat`, `zitten → zij zit`, `wachten → hij wacht`.
- A stem that ends in **d** does get the t, although you cannot hear it: `worden → hij wordt`, `vinden → zij vindt`. (Unit B1 · 13 is all about this.)

### Jij after the verb: no t

When the subject `jij` or `je` comes directly **after** the verb, the t disappears. That happens in questions and whenever the sentence starts with something other than the subject.

> Jij begint vroeg. — You start early.
> Begin jij altijd zo vroeg? — Do you always start this early?
> Morgen werk je thuis. — Tomorrow you are working from home.

This is only true for jij and je. `Hij` and `u` keep their t: `Werkt hij vandaag?`, `Werkt u hier?`

### Watch out

- The ik-form is the bare stem: `ik werk`, never *ik werkt or *ik werken.
- The t of hij and zij is part of the spelling even where fast speech swallows it: `hij werkt`, never *hij werk.
- Write the stem as a Dutch word: `ik reis`, not *ik reiz; `ik maak`, not *ik mak; `ik stop`, not *ik stopp.
- `Wij`, `jullie` and plural `zij` take the infinitive: `wij werken`, never *wij werkt.

### Compared with Ukrainian

Ukrainian has a different ending for every person (`працюю, працюєш, працює…`), so the pronoun can be left out. Dutch has only three forms, and the subject must always be there: `Працюю вдома` is `Ik werk thuis`, never just *Werk thuis.

sentences.nl: Ik werk op een kantoor in Utrecht.
sentences.en: I work in an office in Utrecht.
sentences.note: The ik-form is the bare stem: werken → werk, with no ending.

sentences.nl: Mijn collega begint elke dag om acht uur.
sentences.en: My colleague starts at eight o'clock every day.
sentences.note: Mijn collega is a hij/zij-subject: stem + t. The stem of beginnen is begin, with one n.
alt: Elke dag begint mijn collega om acht uur.

sentences.en: We usually have a meeting on Mondays.
sentences.note: With wij the verb is simply the infinitive: vergaderen.

sentences.en: The boss sends a lot of messages.
sentences.note: sturen → stem stuur: the long u is written double once -en is gone. Then + t for de baas.

sentences.nl: Reis jij vaak voor je werk?
sentences.en: Do you often travel for your work?
sentences.note: reizen → stem reis (z becomes s). Jij comes directly after the verb, so there is no t.
alt: Reis je vaak voor je werk?

sentences.en: What time do you stop today?
sentences.note: stoppen → stem stop, with one p. Je follows the verb, so the t is dropped: stop je.

sentences.nl: Zij regelt alle afspraken voor ons.
sentences.en: She arranges all the appointments for us.
sentences.note: regelen → stem regel, + t for zij (she). The plural zij would be: zij regelen.
alt: Ze regelt alle afspraken voor ons.

sentences.nl: In de pauze praat ik met mijn collega's.
sentences.en: During the break I talk to my colleagues.
sentences.note: praten → stem praat: the long a is doubled. The ik-form has no ending, wherever ik stands in the sentence.
alt: Ik praat in de pauze met mijn collega's.
Tijdens de pauze praat ik met mijn collega's.
Ik praat tijdens de pauze met mijn collega's.

sentences.en: Are you (formal) working from home tomorrow too?
sentences.note: U keeps its t in a question. Only jij and je lose it after the verb.

sentences.nl: Hij leest zijn berichten in de trein.
sentences.en: He reads his messages on the train.
sentences.note: lezen → stem lees: z becomes s and the long e is doubled. Then + t for hij.
alt: In de trein leest hij zijn berichten.
Hij leest in de trein zijn berichten.

exercises.note: Wij takes the infinitive: beginnen. Begin is the ik-form, begint the form for jij, u, hij and zij.

exercises.nl: Mijn collega ___ elke dag met de trein.
exercises.en: My colleague travels by train every day.
exercises.note: The stem of reizen is reis: at the end of a word the z becomes s. Mijn collega is a hij/zij-subject, so stem + t: reist.

exercises.en: Are you working at the office today?
exercises.note: Jij stands directly after the verb, so the t disappears: Werk jij? With hij or u it would stay: Werkt hij? Werkt u?

exercises.nl: Ik ___ elke ochtend koffie voor mijn collega's.
exercises.en: I make coffee for my colleagues every morning.
exercises.note: maken → stem maak: the a is long, so it is written double once -en is gone. Ik takes the bare stem.

exercises.nl: De baas ___ (sturen) ons elke maandag een lijst met taken.
exercises.en: The boss sends us a list of tasks every Monday.
exercises.note: The stem of sturen is stuur, with the long u doubled. De baas is a hij/zij-subject, so stem + t: stuurt.
lezen → lees: the z becomes s and the long e is doubled. Ik takes the stem without an ending.

exercises.en: What time do you (plural) stop today?
exercises.note: Jullie is plural, so the verb is the infinitive, also in a question: stoppen.

exercises.nl: Je ___ (praten) te veel in de pauze.
exercises.en: You talk too much during the break.
exercises.note: The stem praat already ends in t, and a second t is never added: je praat, hij praat.

exercises.nl: Op drukke dagen ___ (beginnen) ik om zeven uur.
exercises.en: On busy days I start at seven o'clock.
exercises.note: Ik takes the bare stem wherever it stands in the sentence: begin, with one n and without t.

answers: Morgen vergaderen we om twee uur.
Morgen om twee uur vergaderen we.
exercises.en: Tomorrow we have a meeting at two o'clock.
exercises.note: The verb keeps its form wherever the subject stands: we takes the infinitive, vergaderen. (Why the verb comes before we is the subject of unit A2 · 3.)

exercises.en: What time does the meeting start?
exercises.note: After the question words comes the verb, and it agrees with de vergadering: stem + t, begint.

exercises.from: Ik reis elke week naar Brussel.
answers: Hij reist elke week naar Brussel.
exercises.en: He travels to Brussels every week.
exercises.note: Hij needs stem + t. The stem stays reis, with s: reist, never reizt.

exercises.task: Make it a question (start with the verb).
exercises.en: Are you working from home today?
exercises.note: In the question jij comes after the verb, and then the t is dropped: Werk jij?

exercises.wrong: Mijn collega werk op vrijdag thuis.
answers: Mijn collega werkt op vrijdag thuis.
exercises.en: My colleague works from home on Fridays.
exercises.note: Mijn collega is a hij/zij-subject and needs the t: werkt. Werk without t is only for ik, and for jij after the verb.

exercises.wrong: Ik leez elke ochtend mijn berichten.
answers: Ik lees elke ochtend mijn berichten.
exercises.en: I read my messages every morning.
exercises.note: At the end of a word the z becomes s: the stem of lezen is lees. The z only comes back in the plural, wij lezen.
